fixes.explanation: That's what the text says: when Ish-bosheth heard Abner had died in Hebron, "…he lost courage…" Abner was the army commander who had put him on the throne (2 Samuel 2:8-9), so I think the news hit him hard. Picture the one holding your whole plan together suddenly gone. Nobody's knees stay steady after that.

That's right, baker. David's young men "…took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner’s tomb in Hebron." Abner was the commander who made Ish-bosheth king (2 Samuel 2:8-9), so the two ended up together. I think that's a quiet, careful ending to a hard scene.
